stage1.impression: A tight square detail of a dark green translucent box with a rounded grip slot, set against a white void. The slot is a dead black hole. The right edge dissolves into a neon-green bloom that bleeds onto the white. The big faces are flat, waxy and featureless, like denoised plastic, and the lower 40% of the frame is two empty panels. It reads as a competent CG render, not a macro a luxury house would run.

blocking_9: The flat faces need a readable specular gradient from a large source (lum_range of 30 or more across [150,400,1300,600]); today it is 9.6
The grip must read as a cut through 20 mm acrylic, with lit lips and visible depth, not a flat near-black hole (interior lum_range 2.0 today)
The right silhouette must be a crisp glowing edge against the white, with no saturated green halo spreading 100+ px onto the seamless
The frame needs a hierarchy: the grip as the clear subject, with no half-frame of empty panel below it and no cut-off posts at the top as an afterthought
The surfaces need believable micro-texture (cast acrylic with polish marks and subtle variation), not denoised wax

defects.what: A saturated green bloom (g_median 251, r 158, b 126) smears the right edge onto the white seamless. The silhouette edge is about 56 px wide and the structure is unreadable.
The grip interior is uniform near-black (lum 24.6, range 2.0). It shows no depth and no material; it reads as a hole in a texture.
A soft, blotchy bright smear under the slot (p95 150 against 60 around it) that reads as a light leak or denoiser artifact.
The upper face is flat (lum range 9.6) and matte. No reflection of any source describes the plane.
Two empty, flat panels (lum range 3.6 to 4.4) fill the lower 35% of the frame and add nothing.
Two horn posts are cut by the top edge. They read as stray rods, not as a deliberate inclusion.
The top edge band is a blurry, smeared translucent strip with muddy ghosting behind it, and no crisp polished edge line.
The side fin and its two pins are soft and lost inside the green glow.

changes.problem: The back light drives the right edge into a neon-green bloom that bleeds onto the white and smears the silhouette, and it leaks a blotch under the slot.

evidence.measured: g_median 251, r_median 158, b_median 126, lum_median 221.7. The right edge 10-90 width is 56 px. The region under the slot [300,860,1250,930] has a p95 of 150.7.

changes.expected: The right edge reads as a thin, bright, polished green line on clean white. The halo is gone and the fin and pins are legible. The smear under the slot disappears.

changes.problem: The big faces show no reflection, so the acrylic reads as matte plastic and the planes are undescribed.

evidence.measured: lum_range 9.6, median 61.8. The lower panels [150,1100,700,1550] have a range of 4.4.

change.from: azimuth -25, elevation 22, distance 3.0, size [0.4, 2.0], ramp z 0.2 to 1.8
change.to: azimuth 14, elevation 4, distance 3.0, size [1.6, 1.2], ramp z 0.5 to 1.1, values 0 to 1

changes.expected: The panel sits near the camera's mirror angle on the face, so a soft graduated sheen runs top to bottom across the green faces and both lower panels. The faces read as polished cast acrylic.

changes.problem: The grip, which is the subject of the frame, is a dead black hole with no visible depth or cut edges.

change.to: size [0.3, 0.3], orbit azimuth 4, elevation 30, distance 1.8, target [0.12, 0.0, 0.78], irradiance 5.0, color #FFFAF4, specular 1.0

changes.expected: The slot's lower lip and floor catch light, so the 20 mm cut wall shows as a bright band and the interior falls off from the lip into depth.

changes.problem: The frame looks square-on at a flat panel, so the cut has no depth, and half the frame is empty panel below the subject.

evidence.measured: lum_range 3.6 to 4.4 over about 35% of the frame. The grip sits at y 630 to 860.

changes.expected: A slight three-quarter view from above shows the grip's cut walls in perspective and the top edge's polished thickness. The grip moves up to the upper third, with the right silhouette still in frame and less dead panel below.

changes.problem: The denoiser has erased surface micro-detail and leaves blotchy, waxy gradients.

evidence.measured: lum_range 3.6 on a large lit acrylic face, with no grain or texture

change.to: samples 768, adaptive 0.003, clarity 0.07, plus a 0.6% luminance grain in finish

changes.expected: Cleaner gradients without denoise blotches, a little photographic texture, and crisper edges at the slot and the fin.

changes.problem: The glossy flag on the right throws a green-lit reflection into the side fin, which adds to the glow rather than defining it.

evidence.measured: a bright green vertical band inside the fin, merged with the bloom

changes.expected: A dark edge line defines the fin and its pins against the white, separating the product from the background.

changes.problem: The top edge band is a muddy, ghosted strip with no crisp polished edge.

evidence.measured: lum_range 194.9 with soft, smeared transitions and a green ghost of the internal structure

changes.expected: A clean bright line along the top's front edge, from the overhead scrim reflecting in the 20 mm edge, which states the material's thickness.

out_of_scope.request: Give the acrylic faces a real polished cast-acrylic surface response (lower roughness, subtle internal variation) instead of a matte, uniform, waxy shader
out_of_scope.why: This is the product's material, which the card fixes. The matte, uniform faces are the main thing that keeps the image reading as CG.

out_of_scope.request: Clean the internal geometry seen through the top edge (ghosted posts and structure)
out_of_scope.why: These are parts of the speaker, which are fixed.
